question: Febrile non-haemolytic transfusion reactions (FNHTR) are the most dangerous transfusion complication and require immediate cessation of transfusion and full resuscitation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. Febrile non-haemolytic reactions are the most COMMON but not the most dangerous complication. Acute haemolytic transfusion reaction (ABO mismatch) carries the highest mortality and requires immediate cessation and resuscitation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. FNHTR is common but benign; it is caused by recipient antibodies to donor leucocytes. The most dangerous complication is acute haemolytic transfusion reaction (ABO incompatibility), which can cause DIC and death.
